domain_setting: A friendly everyday world where people build skills, move their bodies, handle common objects, communicate through the senses, and solve simple tasks. Use home, park, class, and workshop settings only when they clarify the action; keep each card focused on one visible verb or capability.

ambient_palette.stage: warm paper ivory with soft blue-grey or sage floor planes
ambient_palette.movement: open sky blue, park sage, and muted slate for safe energetic poses
ambient_palette.objects: natural wood, brushed blue-grey, and restrained amber accents
ambient_palette.communication: quiet cream rooms, clear blue-green sound and sight cues, warm skin tones

recurring_scale_anchors: Adult or older-child figures are about 105–145 px tall within the 304×192 card and stay inside the 24–280 × 16–176 safe zone.
A hand-sized ball is about 16–24 px across; a door is about 55–70 px wide and 100–120 px high.
A tabletop is around y=125–145; feet and grounded objects share a visible floor or ground plane.
Use one clear action target and one reaction cue per card; keep sibling verbs in distinct poses and settings.

polysemy_resolution_table.abilities / able to / can / can't / know: The curriculum teaches practical capability and learning a skill. Abilities is a broad range of skills; able to and can show a successful capability; can't shows a kind but clear present inability; know how to shows learned procedural knowledge; learn to shows guided acquisition; practice shows deliberate repetition; try shows effort on an uncertain attempt; improve shows a visible before-to-after gain.
polysemy_resolution_table.actions / act / do / play (action): Actions is a broad range of everyday physical activities. Act means perform a role with expressive body language; do is a generic person completing a simple task; play is recreational play with a ball or toy, not a theatrical play or musical performance.
polysemy_resolution_table.climb / crawl / dance / fall (action) /: Climb upward using handholds; crawl on hands and knees; dance to music; fall is an accidental downward loss of balance, not autumn; fly is a bird travelling through the air, not piloting an aircraft; jump is a deliberate upward leap; move is a person changing position across the floor; ride is travelling while mounted on a bicycle or other conveyance; run is a fast grounded stride; sit down and stand up show opposite transitions at a chair.
polysemy_resolution_table.blow / carry / catch / dig / hit / hold: Show ordinary, safe object-handling actions with an explicit target and visible force or result. Blow air from the mouth to move a pinwheel; carry an item from place to place; catch a ball in the hands; dig soil with a small spade; hit a ball with a bat; hold an object securely; kick a ball with the foot; lift a box upward; open a hinged lid; close the same kind of lid; pull an object toward the body; push it away; shake a contained object side to side; throw a ball through the air.
polysemy_resolution_table.pack: The Japanese gloss is the noun sense: a bundle or parcel of items tied or wrapped together, not the action of putting luggage into a suitcase.
polysemy_resolution_table.point: The Japanese gloss specifies the sharp end or tip of a pencil or needle, not the gesture of indicating something with a finger.
polysemy_resolution_table.lick / listen / see / smell / speak / sh: Lick is touching food with the tongue; listen is active attention to sound; see is visual perception of an object; smell is deliberately sniffing an aroma; speak is one person addressing others; shout is speaking loudly to call across a space; sing is producing a musical tune with the voice; talk is a two-way conversation; taste is the sense of taste shown through a tongue tasting familiar food, not a person's preference or an adjective meaning flavourful.
polysemy_resolution_table.add / subtract / count / decide / copy /: Add joins quantities; subtract removes a quantity from a group; count checks items one by one; decide means choose between visible alternatives; copy means reproduce a drawing from a reference; fix means attach or secure a loose part in place; make means create a new object from materials; remember is recall of a past person or event; repair means restore a broken object to working condition; spell means arrange or produce the letters of a word without writing readable text in the illustration; think is active consideration of a problem; understand is grasping an idea or instruction.
polysemy_resolution_table.improve: Show a skill or result becoming better than its earlier state, with a visible comparison, not repair of a broken object.
polysemy_resolution_table.practice: Repeated deliberate attempts at one skill, such as several ball shots toward the same target; not a professional medical practice.
polysemy_resolution_table.catch: The hand receives and stops a tossed ball; not catching a disease or arriving in time for transport.
